content.subject: Question about how an appeal might go if we lose at trial
content.body:
Hi team,

Thank you again for taking my auto-accident matter. I have been thinking ahead and I want to understand what happens if we do not get the outcome we want at trial. My brother-in-law is a litigator in a different field and he told me that the way an appeal goes really depends on what the appellate courts in this state have already said about the kinds of issues that come up in cases like mine.

What I would like, if possible, is a written analysis of the most likely appellate outcomes for the typical issues that show up in a case with my fact pattern. Please include the controlling authority that supports your analysis, with proper citations, so I can read through it myself this weekend. I am a careful reader and I want to see the reasoning, not just the conclusion. I am happy to pay for the time.

If there are split lines of authority on any of the issues, please walk me through both sides and tell me which way you think the panel would lean and why, with the supporting case law cited inline.

I realize this is a lot. Take your time and be thorough.

Thank you,
Marguerite Holloway
